title: Investigate prefix/backfill entropy causing jagged per-model trendlines in Console
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary: Several customers have reported sudden jagged drops and spikes in per-model token/time-series on Console after late-event backfills. The hypothesis is that late/rate-limited ingest plus non-deterministic prefix stitching produces high-entropy attribution changes that show up as noise in top-model charts and per-route breakdowns. This ticket captures an investigation, repro steps, short-term mitigations for customer-facing dashboards, and a longer-term plan to make late-event attribution idempotent and explainable.

Observed behavior:
- Console per-model trendlines show stepwise discontinuities when a late backfill completes (usually after rate-limit retries or shard replays).
- Top-model lists reorder unexpectedly for hours after a backfill.
- Customers see transient cost estimations and quota usage that don't match raw ledger exports.

Hypothesis and root areas to check:
1) Ingest ordering: events arriving with older timestamps are currently merged using a last-write-wins merge on prefix hashes leading to nondeterministic attribution when sharded merges are concurrent.
2) Rate limit retry fanout: throttled events are retried with different shard-resolution metadata which changes provenance.
3) Aggregation windowing: sliding-window aggregates are sensitive to watermark logic; late events cause re-aggregation but UI smoothing downweights those updates inconsistently.
4) Backfill batching: large backfills create dense corrections that the UI interprets as new usage spikes rather than reconciliations.

Goals:
- Produce reproducible pipeline test that simulates delayed events + rate-limit retries and shows per-model attribution drift.
- Deploy a short-term console UX change: mark data points that were modified by a backfill/late-ingest (visual provenance band) and add a hover explainer.
- Implement deterministic merge semantics for prefix attribution (idempotent merge keys) in the reconciliation job and a compacted change-log to avoid reorder variance.

Reproduction steps (local):
1) Run ingest simulator with two shards; emit events for model A with timestamps t0..t100 and for model B with interleaving.
2) Delay a subset (10%) of events for model A by 3 hours and replay with different retry metadata simulating rate limit backoff.
3) Run current stitcher and aggregation job; capture per-model hourly buckets and compare to expected stable attribution.
4) Toggle new deterministic-merge patch (branch: feature/deterministic-prefix-merge) and re-run; compare diffs.

Metrics to collect:
- number of per-model reorder events (model attribution flips per hour)
- magnitude of token-count delta for top-10 models after backfill
- latency between ingest and final-stable attribution

User-facing mitigation proposal (short-term):
- Add a provenance ribbon on Console charts for the last 72 hours that flags points touched by backfills or late ingestion. Tooltip explains "This point was adjusted by a delayed ingestion/backfill; values may change as reconciliation completes."
- Introduce a confidence band visual that decays over 48 hours for recently adjusted buckets.

Long-term changes (engineering):
- Make prefix attribution merging idempotent by including a deterministic merge-key: (tenant_id, prefix_hash, original_event_id) with canonical normalization applied at ingest.
- Ensure retry path preserves original_event_id and shard hints so replays do not alter provenance metadata.
- Introduce an append-only compacted changelog for reconciliation that can be replayed in order to reproduce state; use that as source-of-truth for Console read queries.
- Rework sliding-window watermark logic to mark re-aggregations as corrections rather than new events for UI aggregation smoothing.

Acceptance criteria:
- Repro script that demonstrates the problem and shows improvement when deterministic merge is enabled (attached as a link).
- PR merging deterministic-merge change for the reconciliation worker with unit and integration tests.
- Console change toggled behind a runtime flag; hover text and provenance ribbon available on staging.
- Post-deploy monitoring: reduced per-model attribution flip-rate by at least 75% in simulated backfills within 72 hours of fix rollout.
